content: Vaginal metronidazole has the potential to harm an unborn baby. Inform your healthcare provider if you are currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Your healthcare provider will determine whether it is safe for you to use vaginal metronidazole during pregnancy or while trying to conceive. Vaginal metronidazole can pass into breast milk. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, notify your healthcare provider. You may need to pump and discard your breast milk while using vaginal metronidazole and for two days after completing the treatment. Avoid consuming alcohol or products containing propylene glycol while using vaginal metronidazole and for at least one day after stopping Nuvesse or three days after stopping Vandazole. This is to prevent potential adverse interactions. Always inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Specifically, discuss if you are using warfarin (Coumadin), disulfiram (Antabuse) within the past two weeks, or lithium (Eskalith, Lithobid), as these may interact with vaginal metronidazole. If you or someone else accidentally uses too much vaginal metronidazole, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of vaginal metronidazole, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and proceed with your regular dosing schedule. Do not use double or extra doses. It is crucial to complete the full prescribed course of treatment, even if your symptoms improve, to reduce the risk of developing resistance to vaginal metronidazole or similar medications. Common side effects of vaginal metronidazole include headache, vaginal itching, stomach pain, nausea, painful or heavy menstrual periods, sore throat, rash, diarrhea, breast pain (with Vandazole), and vaginal yeast infections. Vaginal yeast infections may occur during or after treatment with vaginal metronidazole, but this medication does not treat yeast infections. If you experience symptoms such as vaginal discharge, itching, or discomfort, contact your healthcare provider, as you may require antifungal treatment. Serious side effects, though less common, include severe allergic reactions. Stop using vaginal metronidazole and seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as difficulty breathing, wheezing, rapid heartbeat, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, throat tightness, itching, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, stomach cramps, or joint pain. Nervous system problems have been reported with other forms of metronidazole taken orally or via injection. Stop using vaginal metronidazole and contact your healthcare provider if you experience seizures, numbness, tingling, or pain in the hands or feet (peripheral neuropathy), confusion, difficulty thinking, or behavioral changes. Do not use vaginal metronidazole if you are allergic to metronidazole, Nuvesse, Vandazole, parabens, nitroimidazole derivatives, or any ingredients in the specific product dispensed. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients. Vaginal metronidazole should not be used concurrently with certain medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all medications and supplements you are taking to avoid potential interactions. Do not consume alcohol or foods containing propylene glycol while using vaginal metronidazole, as this can lead to serious side effects. Only use vaginal metronidazole if it has been prescribed to you by a healthcare provider. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Keep vaginal metronidazole out of reach of children. Avoid sexual activity and the use of vaginal products such as tampons or douches while using vaginal metronidazole. This medication is intended for vaginal use only. If it comes into contact with your eyes, rinse them with cool water and contact your healthcare provider. Before using vaginal metronidazole, inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any medications or supplements you are taking. This will help them determine if this medication is appropriate for you. Specifically, discuss any nervous system conditions, such as seizures or peripheral neuropathy, as well as any other medications or supplements you are using. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. The effects of vaginal metronidazole on pregnancy and an unborn baby are not fully known. Your healthcare provider will advise you on whether it is safe to use this medication during pregnancy. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, notify your healthcare provider. Vaginal metronidazole passes into breast milk, and you may need to pump and discard your milk while using the medication and for two days after completing treatment.
